verdicts.corrections:
1. Scope is narrower than "during climbs": with default settings (hero poses on) the belly view needs a near-maximum climb pitch (crossing exists only for pitch > ~1.0 rad; at the 1.25 clamp it starts at ~24.75 m/s) AND high speed (Surge 34, full thumb drag, or trackpad cruise >= ~25). At 8 or 13 m/s the body is nearly upright (+0.13 / +0.11 rad) even at max climb and the back is fully visible; at pitch <= 1.0 rad the back stays visible at every speed up to 34.
2. The visibility criterion is wrong: "view direction dot back-normal > 0" is not the front/back test for a perspective camera; the eye position relative to the body's coronal plane is. The view-dot is already positive at pitch 0.8-1.0 / 34 m/s, yet the GLB raycast shows the spine visible and back-dominant hits there. Using view-dot over-predicts the failure.
3. Cause attribution: the 0.65 climb factor mitigates the problem rather than causing it. The root cause is that pose.lean (-1.35 x streamline) is speed-only and ignores pitch, while climb compensates at most +0.65 rad (velocity alignment at pitch 1.25 needs +1.03). With hero poses off (climb = 0, a saved "classic" option) the belly view appears from ~12.5 m/s at pitch 1.25 and from ~26 m/s at pitch 0.6; reduced motion (factor .25) also fails at 34 m/s.
4. Geometry: at pitch 1.25 the camera is 4.16 m below and 2.34 m behind the root (4.81 / 2.33 relative to the +0.65 head anchor), not "~5 m below and behind".
5. "rotation.x ~ -0.7" holds only at ~34 m/s; it is the lean saturating at -1.35 plus climb +0.65.
6. Full pitch tracking of the boom is intentional (aim/landing reticle, present since the first commit); intentionality does not make the framing acceptable, and no artifact shows the climb framing was ever reviewed.
